reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in transforming deterministic numerical weather prediction (NWP) outputs into calibrated probabilistic forecasts using a Bernstein Quantile Network (BQN). The BQN leverages a 16th-degree Bernstein polynomial to represent quantile functions, ensuring monotonicity through coefficient sorting. This approach avoids the need for ensemble forecasts, relying instead on historical error distributions and joint multi-lead-time training. The model uses 25 input features including 18 NWP-dependent variables and 7 independent ones such as lead time and geographic coordinates. Training occurs over 2019–2020 with testing on 2021 data that includes extreme events, validating robustness. The method is mathematically grounded in quantile regression and calibrated via CRPS normalization. The lead-time embedding mechanism allows for temporal generalization, while the stationarity assumption ensures consistency across forecast horizons. This formulation enables GSE to generate calibrated probabilistic weather states for game-day scenarios without requiring ensemble simulations.
